segments.text: President Nixon speaking with staff.
How much of a chance do you have to talk to Bill?
We're ready for good discussions.
Will he tell him no?
I can't tell you until tomorrow morning.
Oh, not Bill.
What's up?
I got the chance to talk to people.
I even had the chance to talk to my wife.
Don't ever talk to your wife again.
Your wife should never have a veto on important decisions.
Even though marriage is a big count.
Let me tell you what I have in mind, but you can see it in a broader scope than you can describe it.
This is the first, as you know, I've been trying to get you in this administration since the day we arrived,
and you've been very wanted to get you in. I've spent no favor to you, but basically you would help us
We need you around for a number of reasons.
First, you're political. You're highly respected in the government.
You're respected in the press.
And basically, you've learned from some of our more conservative people.
We've learned a lot already.
But I mean, you would help a great deal.
Your point of view would help.
Actually, not beyond this job we want you to do.
But you have done some special things. You've done very well, and I appreciate it.
But basically, Bill, we need you 18 hours a day.
This is culture. And we need you 18 hours a day on probably, although it won't appear that way,
except among the sophisticates and those that can't get gas in the pump.
on the most important single issue that can affect the next 25 years, not only in Africa, but in Europe and Japan
that I hold to today.

and that's what you talk about, you know, even-handedness and so on and so on.

and more of the companies here today.
What I have in mind, Al, is that if Bill does this job, he is the energy man.
Now, you say, nah, I don't care.

That gas cost is too much. We're going to have to use one third of our XM bank money in order to finance it.

So because gas is new to the world, and eventually it isn't,
it'd be to our interest, not only economically, but probably even our interest politically.
We've got to play games there with our Japanese friends to get them sacked.

But we've got to take a hard look at just rushing over things so that you'll realize that you're not doing something practical in each other, which I wouldn't ask you to do, but we can ask you to do it all the rest of the time.

and to the environmentalists, but they'll be dying up there in a few weeks.

Some blood, some blood from this is going to you.

Now, to have the Russians go forward in this and for us not to, it's not only insane.
There's an enormous amount of work in the nuclear energy field that we just left the
that could be done. We've got to push that. Third, coal. They told me, I didn't know this,
that we still have enormous coal deposits in this country and that there are new schemes

Probably way light years ahead, but they're the young ones.
So much of these supplies are demand science stuff.
God knows I don't want to see Russia.

at that point it wouldn't be anything, but several ounces of gallon would be the right amount of labor.
It may be that we have to do something about rations. I hope not. But that's a temporary measure.
And of course all of this is deeply involved in foreign policy. Now how would you fit in?
How you would fit in is, you would be the expert on it.

Bob, you taught me more. You taught me to sign. You taught me to vote. You taught us, and this is very important, that John Conlon, who's our real force, you know, and the only, basically, John Conlon is, represents a lot of clients, but he's totally loyal to try to do what's best for the country, so you can talk to him. And we always set up an outside group, isn't that part of our deal?
Yes, sir. But very, very fluid. We don't want the advisor group to make recommendations that we then have to move away from.
In other words, what I would have thought next, and I'm going to put it to Claire Kennedy, we'd like to have you be the energy czar.
Now, me, I'm worthless. You may be taking a hold of a problem.
committees may blow up, Venezuelans having a little election and they may come to see
the last fight might not get through, we may use more than we expected to, and so on and so forth.
But the whole point is that there is in this world mass supply of cement,
enough to take care of all the needs of air conditioning, even the Congo.

But what is needed is to get those supplies on and what is needed in the United States at the moment is a man who looks at this whole picture and puts it all together so that we speak with one voice and that we have one purpose.
Hey, look, you know you're about as good a guy as you ran the state of Pennsylvania.
This sort of a thing. You'd love it. You really would.
I say 18 hours a day because I'm not speaking for 18 men.
What I'm simply saying is that it's something that requires a concentration of one man
rather than somebody coming in from the outside, in and out.
It just won't work. It won't work if they're in and out.

Because all the employees and woodworkers here are all vying for power, and every time I turn around, Morton's into a plan, you know, he wants to do it, and his plans aren't very good, you know, because, not because of Morton, but because his underwriters really didn't know enough about it. They just wanted to interiorize the dealings.
But there it is. It involves all counts. It involves offshore drilling. It involves taxes. It involves antitrust. And it involves war.
Is that a big enough challenge for you?
It certainly is. I don't want you to go into your arm about crime.
No, no, no. We've been doing very well.
You know what it is. It's this gift. The work that you have done in the foreign peace is in my book. I've written this to you on several occasions.
to be able to decrease American international power and at the same time to be able to enhance
and to live its situation in the world and at the same time be able to understand what
what it's going to be in the future, ahead of everybody else, is what you've done in the last three years, China-Russia.
It's really extraordinary, everybody tells you this, but I think only some of us just think,
oh, so many people are blacked out by Vietnam. Vietnam is going to end one way or the other.
It's time. Well, China and Russia are infinitely more important.
These two books are written, and it will be China and Russia we've done so far.
And now we're in a different position, and you recognize this almost before anybody did.
You told me this, you know, in December of 1967. You may not remember that, but you did
in your apartment in New York.
Well, you called me again in March of 68 when you had me down there again in June of 68.

He said four things. He said we've got to change our relationships with Western Europe because Johnson has nothing to go but forward with one reason or another and he certainly didn't bring back the red folder that has the latest letter version of it.

You told me secondly that it was nonsense for us to continue to be fighting with the Soviets here, the two superpowers, and although we always had to watch them very carefully, we had to come to some kind of accommodation.
You told me thirdly that we had to end the Vietnam War.
And you told me fourthly, and I said you heard me openly, Mr. President, I really wasn't sure that you honestly were going to do it.
We had to open the door to China.
You know, another fellow that remembers that, he might check notes with the Zed Brock.
As I talked to his brother about the China thing, too.
I had thought about China a great deal, and let me tell you, it was much against my instincts.
I didn't want to. I know that.
There's a bit neater as you get, you wouldn't want to, because I know these people.
But what do you do?
If we left, for example, on China Road, could the man sitting in this office today, when our bargaining position is so great that Chinese seem to disperse their own nature from the world they know?
And at a time when there is the most populated nation with one-fourth of potentially the most abled people in the world living there,
When there are many nuclear power, we allow this non-communication and isolation to continue
and let them out there and to open them.
So that fifty years from now, the man sitting in this chair will face a major nuclear power
with ten times the number of people he's got.
No way!
That's what it's all about.

Well, I want you to know that if I take this job, I want this energy policy, as it fits in domestically, and even more importantly, in the long run, as it fits in with the whole international situation, and I want this to be Richard Nixon's policy.
I want to make that very clear to you. It's a natural integration and implementation and follow-up of what you've already done.
And that's what it ought to be.
Well, you're very confident.
No, I'm not. I told you that didn't I, sir, a few minutes ago. I mean every word of it.
It's extremely important that that's the way it be.
you've done this remarkable thing in the last three years and this is a follow-on one of your
three other ones you're doing next week which is just vitally important and you know you gave me
the opportunity of working a little bit with the salt business and i just take my hat off to you
Next week, let me tell you the greatest of confidence. We cannot breach a treaty without weapons. We're not ready.
But we're going to make a great effort.
Our good friend, the State Department Secretary of State,
Mr. Rush, out of Johnson County, is going to negotiate.
But we're going to negotiate.
But this is not the time to make a deal.
I never believe in making a bad deal in a hurry, and you don't either.
Let me say on this thing, too, which I...
Why am I keeping this when I could rest my back?
The point is, I could visualize how,
but as Bill gets into this,
he is cocked to get into the intervention.
You ought to believe your fellow.

Let's face it, I talked about the listeners on the radio the other day, I was amazed to find that we get only 10% of mid-Eastern oil, but it's 80% of Europe's requirements and 90% of Japan's needs, and therefore, we can also, we can say, well, it's just the European, we've got to make it, it doesn't matter, that's what the dams do, it is warm so well today, 56,000, and so I think the energy man, as I see the energy man, he's got to be plopped down there,
right in the middle barrel of the engine, yes, it has to do with the patient.
You know what I'm saying?
I think Henry would be delighted, and I think Bill would be delighted,
but we're wrong. You may continue.
Absolutely, and I'm not going to agree.
You see, that's the problem we have today.
We were thinking of the Bonham, who's a swan of a fine man, you know what I mean?
That's an excellent man.
But the Bonham doesn't have the complete.
This is big, big, big.
You've got to use the diplomacy to say, well, I'm going to build a nuclear power plant, which will produce, have many mountains, and he'll do that better than you like.
But he will not understand the great international forces that have a trust, et cetera, et cetera.
I want an energy policy built that sweeps, where we need the world.
He may not do it again. Talk to Rachel. What do you think about him?
He teased it. And Ron.
And of course that nice little fellow who was striding around and knocking at it.
He's saying, why did you so get canceled this year?
I said, fuck you.
What's that?
What do you think? He got something bad or they think they can knock him over?
And I'm not sure they think anybody better.
I think they'd be likely to come right with him.
What did you think? Or did we get it all?
No, I don't know the reason for it.
It may have something to do with the islands.
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah.
He may have made some low, hard speech like that on the island tonight.
Well, sure not.
See, when you get to the back, all right.
And the Soviets aren't about to get back.
They may have been in the face of those two northern islands.
Nobody lives on the whole.
There are no jackasses or nothing.
But go ahead.

It doesn't mean anything.
And if the boys get together and decide that's what they're going to do,
You just got to break them apart until they've got the bridges.
Because they've got...
Our production is going up and they're building a lot of new refineries.
So we're going to have... They tell me the problem is primary refineries.
But I'm no expert. That's the thing you've got to do.
Then we have to deal with the process of getting the R&D out so we can do these other things.
And so that's how we deal with the R&D part of the first building.
We're going to put this into the Saturday Announcement, we're going to have some voluntary
conservation measures and some bureaucratic ones that we can impose on our own people,
But then we've got to develop more.
This is...

What in the devil is the matter with us?

I know...

The situation in New York is such that if they don't have that plant, they're not going to have much of a deal with it.

And Maryland, in the county ethics agreement, keep it going so that the reserves in the mid-Atlantic states are reduced to less than two percent.

but it deprives us and the Senate of having about a fourth or third of the House on the floor.

but they won't, and it's terribly important, which I, I would say this,

It doesn't make any difference.

You are considered to be a man of absolute integrity.

to move to

I want you to be very close to me, understand. And my views are probably very close to yours.
But I want you to be out there fighting the battle for, you know, for this country, for this province, and so forth.
Let the chips fall where they may.
You're going to have another problem. You're going to have to fight it.
But I think you've got more in the eyes of the country than I have.
I get along with them pretty well.

to get along with the, you know, and so it's a politician's job, it's a politician's job,
a politician who understands the nature of the problem.

What I would like to do is to have Bill in a smaller group of people, because I'd like to have him in, not because of energy, but because he'd like to sit around.
players, Al Davis, we'll have Bryce, that's about all, and we just sit around and kick

coming up now in the summer period, and we can't handle these on the in and out of Emmerich
tonight, which you will find, and there's a lot of actually very rare chances, I don't

we will make the progress that you have made in clear passing your objection.
If I cannot, I will not have some Congress for 8 and 12 December.

Sir, if you haven't got any commitments to Israel that are going to fill us in the Arab States, let's talk about Israel.
I guess the three of us should talk about Israel.
Every time you talk about Israel, you raise some things.
with a lot of domestic, of our domestic Jewish people, which I have a few, you have perhaps more.
Second, it's an area where Henry, who is Jewish, is not trusted by the Arabs.
I do trust him, but Henry is susceptible to his resurrection.
He's susceptible to it.
They put the country first, and I'm pretty certain that he is, and he knows it.
Third, I am the first president in this office since Israel was recognized as a state.
I've done everything and I have their confidence up to this point, but now we have come to
the moment of truth and I can assure you that on this one we are going to do what we right
now.
It's a very tough one because it's going to require a squeeze on them at a perfect
I don't have a preference about why we should use the Egyptians, what's got to happen here in the inner and southern part of the country.
It's a general question as well.
But the main thing I want you to know is that as far as everyone is concerned, they come in here and say,
well, look, we have elections in October. Now that's there. Good God.
And then we'll have elections in November, and that'll be another argument.
There's an election every year. But we cannot let the Mideast revolution flow.
I feel strongly about it, let me tell you.
The other thing is, I think the American Jewish community has overplayed its hand.
Take, for example, the Israeli exit program that's from Russia.
We've got everything on the Russian people.
I'm sure the Russians need it.
But, Bill, you can't ask the Russians to dismantle their system.
I mean, the thing the Senate wanted me to prove was to say that the Russians,
would allow all minority groups who wanted to leave free exodus to run it.
Well, that would have to be Russia. You'd have 40 million Ukrainians to take off.
Really? Of course you can't do that.
And on the Israeli thing, I totally agree with the Jewish person there.
If you, if you, as a result of your insistence on this writer, on this bill, on Labor Nations,
if you destroy it, you will be responsible for destroying the greatest opportunity for
a more peaceful world and more possible reduction of violence than we have had in our time.
And I am willing to say so.
I don't want to really understand this, but I'll do it if they do that.
Would you be secure? I'm not going to tell you.
Because they can go too far.
And we've got to have a secure history.
No, no, no. I can share with them.
Israel is going to be secure.
We'll give them a guarantee.
Probably the Russians.
We've gone all the way with Israel.
How do you feel about that?
God, we just can't.
They have got to get reasonable.
We couldn't have done more for them than we've done.
I give them every chance that I've promised.
When I say I have.
This country will have this country.
And they trust me.
But they must not have the paper
that now, because of what we've done,
we can do it forever.
I keep telling Mrs. Mayer,
I said to Madam Prime Minister,
time is not a mere sign.
I said, you can look at the whole Arab world today, you can look at five years from now, you can look at ten years from now, twenty-five years from now, twenty years from now, they will have it all.
So move now, make the best of it you can.
And I said, also, Madam Prime Minister, there's another thing.
You can live unless the Russians send in technicians, pilots, etc.
And then you're dead. Unless the United States holds the ground.
It was a tough problem.
What's happened to the Shah?
I don't know what the devil is.
Where is he?
Well that's because other people are making good people.
And the shots were great. Just a couple of times.
He's a very tough guy.
He knows he's going to push for it.
He's very tough, but we have something going for us there to support him.
Very friendly to me.
Very highly amused.
Very highly amused.
I remember when he sent me over down.
I had those four hours with him.
That became extremely clear several months.
And I think he's doing a damn good job getting the Persian Gulf in order too.
Getting it in order.
And also the Gulf.
And getting it around the target.
He's got land, rig, water, everything.
That country.
Tierra Rock is...
I was there in 1953.
And briefly another time in 67.
But today that place is blue in my world.
That's why we had that second highest percentage increase in gross national product in the last 12 years, next to Japan and the world.
This is a very enlightening comment.
Bill, let me say this. It would be a great service to your country if you could just say,
I am not so uncandid as to say that I would appreciate a person.
Because I think you need to. You need to very much.
There are other reasons. And third, I think he would like it. I mean, I think he would like the challenge.
The other thing is that the way I envision the job, it's not just sitting over there in that UOP and pounding around.
I'm not sure what he's got in his feet and whether or not the farmer's out to pick the nut or harvest the grains.
What I have in mind is this big picture that you're assigning to an administrative committee,
including the people, out in the government.
You've got to use the people in the government.
They all are in it, and they're so sensitive about it.
You do that, can't you?
And it will come together.
And what I mean is, cabinet officers, as you know, they're very sensitive about it.
They're pushing it.
They have the right to crowd them.
They've been appointed.
They're running it.
And I think you have that skill where you can let them think they're running what you're running.
That's what really happens.
They run the thing, but the basic strategy decisions have to be made here.
And that's right. I don't want that.
I want you to come in and tell me.
But at least I'll have, I may have some judgments on some things due to the fact that I am somewhat familiar with international situations.
I have, but lately I don't know anything about situations like that.
A little about oil wells.
I did a little bit of work as a lawyer, but that's not all.
And that's changed so much that we even think of a well that was 4,000 feet deep was a hell of a well.
Now they go down to 25,000 feet.
You know, we grow, I set up a company once where we had a pretty good well that made us money.
And we, we incorporated it in there. Those are for $25,000. $25,000 per month.
And today, these guys are talking about millions going well. Right?
Well, good luck to Mr. Brexman, sir.
Right. You can let us know tomorrow.
I will.
